def: Text that makes a model follow instructions from an untrusted source instead of, or alongside, the instructions of the application's developer.
An injection typed by the user of the application in their own message.
An injection planted by a third party in content, such as a web page, email or document, that the application later feeds to the model.
An input that gets a model to ignore its own safety training and produce content that its provider or developer prohibits.
A direct injection that redirects a model away from its assigned task to the attacker's task.
Extracting the hidden system prompt or other instructions a developer gave the model.
A jailbreak failure mode in which the model's drive to follow instructions overrides its trained refusal.
A jailbreak failure mode in which a model's capabilities cover inputs, such as rare languages or encodings, that its safety training did not.
A jailbreak that places a long fake dialogue of compliant answers in the prompt before the real request, becoming more effective as the number of examples grows.
An attack designed with knowledge of a specific defence and refined using its responses, as opposed to a fixed list of known attack strings.
The fraction of attack attempts that achieve the attacker's goal, defined by an observable effect and reported with the attacker's budget.
A training approach that teaches a model to give developer instructions priority over user text and third-party content when they conflict.
Transforming untrusted input so that it carries a signal of its origin, helping a model treat it as data rather than instructions.
